hero.headline: Trump names Bill Pulte as acting director of national intelligence
hero.body:
President Trump has named Bill Pulte, the head of the Federal Housing Finance Agency, to serve as acting director of national intelligence, replacing Tulsi Gabbard who recently left the role.

Pulte, heir to the PulteGroup home construction fortune, has no known experience in national security or intelligence matters. He currently oversees the Federal Housing Finance Agency, which regulates the federal housing lenders Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac. Trump stated that Pulte will retain his housing agency position while taking on the intelligence director role.

"William has deep experience managing the most sensitive matters in America," Trump said on his Truth Social platform, though Pulte's background is primarily in real estate and housing finance rather than intelligence or national security.

The appointment has drawn sharp criticism from several quarters. Senate Majority Leader John Thune expressed concern about Pulte's suitability, telling reporters that "we need professionals there" and warning that Pulte would have "a lengthy road ahead of him" if Trump nominates him permanently, which would require Senate confirmation and hearings. Thune also cautioned against having a "weaponized" intelligence director.

Senator Cassidy stated publicly that Pulte lacks the competence required for the intelligence director role.

Critics have highlighted concerns about Pulte's tenure at the housing agency. Since taking over the Federal Housing Finance Agency, he has made extraordinary allegations against Trump's political opponents, accusing Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook and others of mortgage fraud. Cook has denied the allegations. One former high-ranking official described his handling of the Cook case as "very bizarre."

Pulte has also faced scrutiny for his family connections. Though often described as part of the PulteGroup empire due to his family ties, the New York Times reported that Pulte no longer holds any official position with the company, having been pushed off its board in 2020. The Pulte Family Charitable Foundation, which his aunt and father run, publicly distanced itself from him in 2023, stating that "Bill Pulte is not a representative of, nor has he served in any capacity" for the foundation.

The director of national intelligence oversees the entire U.S. intelligence community, coordinating the work of agencies including the CIA, NSA, and FBI. The position normally requires Senate confirmation, though acting directors can serve temporarily without it. The intelligence director is responsible for briefing the president on national security threats and managing relationships with foreign intelligence services.

Gabbard's departure from the role came after a turbulent tenure in which she appeared marginalized as Trump pursued aggressive foreign policy actions against Venezuela and Iran. According to multiple sources, Trump had been asking cabinet members as early as April about replacing her.

cards.headline: US Military Fires Missile at Iran-Bound Oil Tanker in Gulf
cards.body:
The US military struck an oil tanker headed to Iran, hitting the vessel's engine room after the crew ignored repeated warnings, according to military officials. The action represents a significant escalation in tensions between the United States and Iran amid ongoing regional hostilities.

In a separate incident, Iran claimed responsibility for an attack on a container ship near Iraq's Umm Qasr port. A Panama-flagged MSC vessel was struck by projectiles, causing a large explosion and igniting a fire. The attack on the cargo ship represents one of several recent incidents in Gulf waters as regional conflicts intensify.

The dual incidents highlight growing risks to commercial shipping in the Gulf region. Attacks on vessels have increased as Iran and its regional adversaries engage in escalating military actions. The shipping industry has raised concerns about the safety of cargo vessels and tanker traffic in the strategic waterway, which carries a substantial portion of global oil supplies.

The escalation comes amid broader regional tensions. The entry of Houthi forces from Yemen into direct conflict with Israel marks a dangerous expansion of the fighting. The Iran-aligned militant group fired ballistic missiles at Israeli military sites on Saturday, with military spokesperson Yahya Saree vowing to continue operations until Israel "ceases its attacks and aggression." Israel reported intercepting one missile from Yemen.

The Houthis' involvement poses a direct threat to the Bab al-Mandab strait at the southern end of the Red Sea, a critical chokepoint for global energy supplies and trade. Combined with Iran's actions affecting the Strait of Hormuz, any further disruptions could severely impact the global economy. Saudi commentators have warned that if alternative pipeline routes through Saudi Arabia become threatened, Riyadh could enter the conflict directly.

Pakistan has attempted to mediate the dispute, with the country's foreign minister announcing that Iran agreed to allow additional Pakistani-flagged vessels through the Strait. Pakistani officials have also arranged talks between Middle Eastern powers, though none of the actively warring parties are participating, raising questions about the effectiveness of diplomatic efforts.

The conflict has expanded in scope and weaponry. Reports indicate cluster munitions were used in strikes near an Iranian missile base, according to experts cited by Bellingcat. While the US is the only party in the conflict to possess these weapons, Iran has used ballistic missiles carrying cluster warheads in its strikes.

Ukraine has become an indirect participant, signing defense agreements with the United Arab Emirates and Qatar while providing anti-drone technology and expertise to Gulf states. The country's president announced these agreements after similar pacts with Saudi Arabia were established.

As the conflict enters its second month, Pakistan continues seeking to broker talks between the US and Iran, though officials have made conflicting claims about whether such discussions have already begun.

cards.headline: Israel Continues Lebanon Strikes as Peace Talks Resume in Washington
cards.teaser: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu vowed to continue operations against Hezbollah even as officials met for negotiations.
cards.body:
Israeli and Lebanese officials held peace talks in Washington while Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu reaffirmed Israel's commitment to continuing military operations against Hezbollah. Israel has maintained strikes in southern Lebanon but has avoided attacking Beirut following a US-announced deal.

The partial truce in the south appears to be holding despite ongoing Israeli military operations in the region. The parallel diplomatic and military efforts represent a fragile attempt to move toward a broader ceasefire agreement.

cards.headline: Canada Requests 16-Year Renewal of North American Trade Pact
cards.teaser: Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc wrote to US and Mexican counterparts proposing to renew the USMCA deal.
cards.body:
Canada formally requested a 16-year renewal of the USMCA trade agreement, with Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc sending a letter to his US and Mexican counterparts proposing the extension of the North American free trade pact.

The renewal proposal came as LeBlanc met with the US Trade Representative. The timing coincided with recent comments from President Trump referring to Canada as the 51st state ahead of the trade discussions.

cards.headline: Thousands of sailors remain trapped by Strait of Hormuz blockade
cards.teaser: About 20,000 seafarers have been stuck in the Iran war zone for months.
cards.body:
Approximately 20,000 seafarers remain trapped by a blockade in the Strait of Hormuz, unable to leave the war zone. The sailors have been stuck for months as the situation continues.

The prolonged uncertainty has caused significant stress and exhaustion among the trapped crew members. The strait is a critical waterway for global shipping, and the blockade has left merchant vessels and their crews unable to transit safely.

cards.headline: Treasury Sanctions Iran's Largest Cryptocurrency Exchange
cards.teaser: The US imposed sanctions on Nobitex and several executives for allegedly helping Iran evade sanctions and finance militants.
cards.body:
The US Treasury Department sanctioned Nobitex, Iran's largest cryptocurrency exchange, along with several of its executives. The Treasury accused the platform of enabling the Iranian government to circumvent existing sanctions and finance militant groups operating in the region.

The action represents part of the US government's broader strategy to constrain Iran's financial capabilities and limit its ability to support proxy forces abroad.

cards.headline: Justice Department ends Trump anti-weaponization fund
cards.teaser: Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche confirmed the $1.8 billion fund will not move forward.
cards.body:
The Justice Department has abandoned plans for a $1.8 billion fund intended to compensate Trump's allies who claimed to be targets of government weaponization. Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche announced the decision during a House appropriations committee hearing, stating the administration is "not moving forward with the fund, period."

Despite scrapping the fund, the Justice Department is maintaining a separate agreement that prohibits the IRS from auditing Trump, his family, and related entities. Blanche acknowledged that concerns about government weaponization remain valid, but the administration determined the compensation fund would not proceed.

cards.teaser: Iran claimed responsibility for striking a Panama-flagged MSC vessel with projectiles, causing an explosion and fire.
cards.body:

The strike ignited a fire on the MSC ship. The attack represents an escalation in regional maritime hostilities as Iran conducts military operations in Gulf waters.

cards.headline: Court Delays US Ebola Quarantine Unit Plans in Kenya
cards.teaser: A Kenyan court ruling further delayed the Trump administration's proposed facility for Americans exposed to the virus.
cards.body:
A Kenyan court has delayed the Trump administration's plans to establish a quarantine facility for Americans exposed to Ebola. The proposed site is located at Laikipia Air Base in Nanyuki, approximately 120 miles from Nairobi.

The plan has faced significant local opposition. Residents of the area argue that Kenya should not accept foreign quarantine patients, citing concerns about disease exposure in a country with no known Ebola cases. Local community members view the proposal as indicative of double standards, believing that quarantine should occur in citizens' home countries rather than placing the burden on Kenya.

cards.headline: British Police Under Investigation for Handcuffing Dying Stabbing Victim
cards.teaser: Authorities are investigating officers who restrained student Henry Nowak while he was dying from stab wounds.
cards.body:
British authorities are investigating police officers who handcuffed Henry Nowak, a student who was dying from stab wounds. Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer said the footage raises serious questions for police and called for an examination of how "accusations of racism informed decision making" in the incident.

The case has sparked significant public outrage in the UK, with protesters clashing with police in Southampton. The incident has prompted scrutiny of police procedures for responding to stabbing victims and their conduct at crime scenes.

cards.headline: Protests Intensify in Albania Over Kushner-Linked Resort Development
cards.teaser: Plans for luxury resorts on the Adriatic Sea have become a flashpoint for frustrations with the government.
cards.body:
Protests in Albania have grown over plans for luxury resort developments on the Adriatic Sea linked to Kushner. The projects have long worried environmentalists concerned about coastal development.

The resort plans have become a flashpoint for broader public frustrations with the Albanian government. Demonstrators have used the development controversy to express wider grievances about government policies and decision-making.

cards.headline: California votes in governor primary election
cards.teaser: Xavier Becerra has leapfrogged rivals in a crowded field with a clear top three candidates.
cards.body:
California held its primary election for governor during the state's midterm election cycle. Xavier Becerra emerged as the establishment favorite, positioning himself as a traditional Democrat who would continue corporate-friendly policies. However, the race presented Democrats with a significant choice about the direction of the party in the deep-blue state.

The primary determined which candidates would advance to the general election, with multiple contenders competing for position. The outcome would shape California's governance of the world's fourth-largest economy.

cards.headline: Thousands of sailors remain trapped by Strait of Hormuz blockade
cards.teaser: About 20,000 seafarers have been stuck in the Iran war zone for months.

cards.headline: Hostage situation unfolds at California Chase Bank
cards.teaser: Police are negotiating with a suspect at a bank in downtown Bakersfield amid a bomb threat.
cards.body:
Police in Bakersfield are responding to a hostage situation at a Chase Bank location in the downtown area. The incident involves a bomb threat that prompted evacuations of nearby buildings, including City Hall.

Law enforcement is conducting negotiations with the suspect. Police have stated that community members inside the bank are safe. The situation led to lockdowns at multiple downtown buildings as authorities work to resolve the incident.

cards.headline: Los Angeles holds mayoral primary election
cards.teaser: Bass, Pratt, and Raman are competing in the primary to lead the city.
cards.body:
Los Angeles conducted its mayoral primary election with three main candidates competing for the position. Bass, Spencer Pratt, and Raman faced off in the race to determine who will advance to lead the nation's second-largest city.

Pratt, known for appearing on the reality show "The Hills" with Heidi Montag, has made the transition from entertainment to politics. The primary results will determine which candidates move forward to the general election.

cards.headline: Warmer summer forecast increases likelihood of heatwaves
cards.teaser: Long-range forecasts predict warmer and drier conditions compared to average.
cards.body:
Summer weather forecasts indicate temperatures will be above normal, increasing the probability of multiple heatwaves in the coming months. The forecasts also predict drier conditions than average across affected regions.

Long-range predictions have been issued to help communities and emergency services prepare for the warmer-than-normal pattern expected over the summer period.

hero.headline: Colorado Tightens Oversight of Uber and Lyft Following Sexual Assault Reports
hero.body:
Colorado enacted legislation requiring stricter scrutiny of ride-sharing companies Uber and Lyft. The law responds to findings that these companies received far more reports of sexual assault and misconduct than they had publicly disclosed.

The legislation cites a New York Times investigation that uncovered the discrepancy between the number of sexual assault and sexual misconduct reports Uber received and what the company shared with the public. The investigation revealed a pattern of underreporting that raised concerns about passenger safety and corporate transparency in the ride-sharing industry.

Under the new law, Colorado will impose additional regulatory requirements on ride-sharing platforms operating in the state. The measure aims to improve accountability and ensure companies provide accurate information about safety incidents to both regulators and the public. The law represents one of the most significant state-level regulatory actions targeting ride-sharing companies in recent years.

The ride-sharing industry has faced mounting pressure to address safety concerns, particularly regarding incidents of sexual assault and harassment involving drivers and passengers. Companies have implemented various safety features in recent years, including in-app emergency buttons and background checks for drivers, but critics argue these measures have not gone far enough.

Colorado's action could set a precedent for other states considering similar legislation. Ride-sharing companies operate in a patchwork of state and local regulations across the country, with safety standards varying significantly by jurisdiction. The new Colorado law adds to growing momentum for stronger oversight of the industry at the state level.

The Colorado legislation comes at a time when ride-sharing platforms face scrutiny on multiple fronts. Beyond safety concerns, drivers have also raised complaints about compensation and working conditions. As fuel prices have risen significantly in recent months, independent contractors working for these platforms have expressed frustration about inadequate support from their employers.

Drivers across the country have reported that rising fuel costs have substantially cut into their earnings without corresponding increases in pay from Uber and Lyft. The companies have responded by expanding discount programs and rewards through financial services products, though drivers have expressed skepticism about the effectiveness of these measures.

The Colorado law specifically addresses sexual assault and misconduct reporting, requiring companies to maintain higher transparency standards with both state regulators and the general public. By mandating stricter oversight, the state aims to hold ride-sharing platforms accountable for accurately disclosing safety incidents rather than minimizing or hiding them from public view.

As more states consider implementing similar regulations, the ride-sharing industry faces the prospect of increasingly fragmented regulatory requirements across different jurisdictions. Companies operating nationally will need to adapt their safety protocols and reporting procedures to comply with varying state standards. Colorado's approach reflects broader concerns about corporate accountability and passenger protection in the rapidly evolving gig economy.

cards.headline: Shipping Vessel Struck by Projectiles at Iraqi Port
cards.teaser: A Mediterranean Shipping Company vessel was attacked while in an Iraqi port, highlighting continued risks to commercial shipping.
cards.body:
A vessel owned by the Mediterranean Shipping Company was struck by two projectiles while at an Iraqi port. The attack occurred as the United States and Iran work to negotiate the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.

The incident underscores ongoing threats to commercial shipping in the region despite diplomatic efforts. The Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for global oil shipments, has been a focal point of tensions affecting maritime trade routes.

cards.headline: Microsoft Tests Wearable AI Device for Office Workers
cards.teaser: The company is internally testing a wearable access badge and desktop device designed for workplace use.
cards.body:
Microsoft announced that its employees are testing a wearable access badge integrated with artificial intelligence capabilities. The company is also evaluating a desktop device as part of the same initiative.

The devices are aimed at office workers and represent Microsoft's exploration of AI-enabled hardware for the workplace. The company has not disclosed when or if the products will become commercially available beyond the current employee testing phase.

cards.headline: Victoria's Secret Shares Reach Record High on Strong Sales
cards.teaser: The retailer's stock climbed to an all-time high as its revised product strategy drove performance.
cards.body:
Victoria's Secret shares hit a record high following strong sales results. The company's focus on bra products powered a turnaround that exceeded Wall Street expectations and led the retailer to issue upbeat annual forecasts.

The stock surged approximately 50 percent as the chain outperformed competitors in the retail sector. The company's strategy shift appears to have resonated with consumers, marking a significant reversal for the brand.

cards.headline: Ulta Beauty Raises Earnings Outlook After Beating Expectations
cards.teaser: The beauty retailer reported stronger than expected results and increased its full-year profit forecast.
cards.body:
Ulta Beauty beat Wall Street expectations for its fiscal first quarter and raised its earnings outlook for the full year. The company reported revenue growth across multiple channels and product categories.

Shares of the beauty retailer rose following the announcement. The results showed continued consumer spending on beauty products and successful execution across Ulta's business operations.

cards.headline: Remote Work Linked to Job Struggles for Recent College Graduates
cards.teaser: Research indicates that the shift to remote work, rather than artificial intelligence, is making it harder for new graduates to find employment.
cards.body:
New research from the Federal Reserve Bank of New York found that remote work has contributed to difficulties recent college graduates face when seeking employment. The study contradicts assumptions that artificial intelligence is the primary factor behind youth unemployment challenges.

The research suggests that the prevalence of remote work arrangements has reduced opportunities for entry-level workers who traditionally benefited from in-person training and networking. Multiple studies have reached similar conclusions about the impact of work-from-home policies on new graduate hiring.

cards.headline: Senate Democrats Oppose Cryptocurrency in 401(k) Plans
cards.teaser: Senators Bernie Sanders and Elizabeth Warren urged the Labor Department to reject proposals allowing digital assets in retirement accounts.
cards.body:
Senate Democrats are opposing a Labor Department proposal that would allow 401(k) retirement plans to include cryptocurrency, private credit, and private equity investments. In a letter shared with the Guardian, Bernie Sanders, Elizabeth Warren, and House Education and Workforce Committee ranking member Bobby Scott argued the rule would expose an estimated $14.2 trillion in retirement savings to volatile and complex assets.

The Democrats contend the change poses significant financial risks to workers and claim the rule would likely face legal challenges. Their opposition joins concerns from state officials and reflects broader Democratic skepticism about expanding access to cryptocurrency within retirement accounts.

hero.headline: Microsoft launches AI assistant designed to work as always-on office companion
hero.body:
Microsoft introduced Scout, a new artificial intelligence assistant designed to function as a constant workplace companion for office workers. The software giant unveiled the product at its Build developer conference, positioning it as an autonomous agent that operates continuously rather than requiring manual activation.

Internal Microsoft documents reveal the company aims to make users dependent on the new tool. The documents state Microsoft wants to "make people addicted" to Scout, which represents a shift in how the company frames AI deployment in professional settings. The assistant is built on technology called OpenClaw and functions differently from traditional software by working autonomously rather than waiting for user commands.

Scout operates as what Microsoft calls a personal agent, designed to handle tasks typically managed by executive assistants. The system remains active constantly, monitoring workflows and responding to needs without requiring users to open specific applications or issue direct commands. Microsoft is also developing Project Solara, an Android-based operating system designed specifically for AI agents rather than traditional mobile applications.

The launch represents Microsoft's broader strategy to embed AI throughout its business products. The company also announced new AI models intended to reduce its dependence on OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT in which Microsoft holds a significant investment. The new models aim to lower costs for developers building AI-powered applications on Microsoft's platform.

Microsoft is testing a wearable AI device aimed at office workers alongside the Scout software. The hardware component would extend the AI assistant's reach beyond computer screens, though specific details about the wearable's capabilities remain limited. The dual approach of software and hardware reflects Microsoft's effort to compete in a market where multiple technology companies are racing to deploy AI tools that integrate into daily work routines.

cards.headline: Lawsuit claims Ring cameras scan faces of visitors and passersby without consent
cards.teaser: Amazon-owned Ring faces legal action over allegations its cameras use AI to identify faces of guests and people walking past homes.
cards.body:
Ring, the home security camera company owned by Amazon, is facing a lawsuit alleging its devices scan the faces of visitors and passersby without authorization. The legal complaint claims Ring cameras use artificial intelligence to identify people who appear in the camera's field of view, including guests arriving at homes and pedestrians walking past.

The lawsuit seeks compensation for Americans whose faces were scanned by the system. Ring cameras are installed at millions of homes across the country, positioned at doorways and perimeters where they capture footage of anyone who approaches or passes by the property.

cards.headline: Apple preparing major overhaul of Siri and AI features for iOS 27
cards.teaser: Apple will preview updates to its voice assistant and artificial intelligence capabilities at its developer conference on June 8.
cards.body:
Apple plans to introduce significant changes to Siri and its AI features in iOS 27, which the company will preview at its Worldwide Developers Conference starting June 8. The updates represent one of Apple's largest AI-focused initiatives as the company faces increasing pressure to compete with rivals in artificial intelligence.

The conference will include announcements about new iPhone software alongside the Siri improvements. The event marks what analysts describe as Apple's biggest AI test, with the company's strategy in machine learning under scrutiny from investors and customers who have watched competitors release AI products over the past year.

cards.headline: Cybersecurity startup Cyera nearing $300 million funding at $12 billion valuation
cards.teaser: The company is raising capital at 80 times its annual recurring revenue despite posting operating losses.
cards.body:
Cyera, a cybersecurity company, is close to completing a $300 million funding round led by Evolution Equity Partners that would value the business at $12 billion. The valuation represents 80 times the company's annual recurring revenue, a premium multiple in the venture capital market.

The funding round proceeds despite Cyera reporting operating losses. High valuation multiples based on revenue rather than profitability have become more common among fast-growing enterprise software companies, particularly those in the cybersecurity sector where investors anticipate long-term growth.

cards.headline: DIY cyberdeck computers gain popularity as alternative to mainstream tech devices
cards.teaser: Custom-built portable computers designed by hobbyists are attracting attention on social media as users seek alternatives to corporate technology.
cards.body:
Cyberdecks, custom-built portable computers assembled by individuals rather than manufactured by technology companies, have grown rapidly in popularity over recent months. Users share designs on social media for solar-powered game emulators, pocket-sized e-readers, and clamshell computers built into purses or other unconventional cases.

The trend reflects a desire among some technology users to avoid corporate surveillance and regain control over their computing devices. DIY hardware communities building these machines have expanded significantly, with participants sharing instructions and designs for creating personalized computers from scratch using off-the-shelf components.

---

Note: The provided source material covers unrelated topics (Aukus submarine technology and Anthropic's IPO plans) and contains no information about cyberdecks. The original card text has been returned unchanged.

cards.headline: MSI releasing Claw 8 EX gaming handheld on June 23
cards.teaser: The portable gaming device uses Intel's new Arc G3 graphics chip designed specifically for handheld systems.
cards.body:
MSI will release the Claw 8 EX AI+ gaming handheld on June 23. The device features Intel's Arc G3 Series graphics processor, which Intel developed specifically for portable gaming rather than adapting chips designed for laptops.

The handheld represents MSI's effort to compete in the growing market for portable gaming devices. Intel created the Arc G3 as purpose-built silicon for gaming handhelds rather than using modified versions of its standard mobile processors, aiming to deliver better performance in the compact form factor.

cards.headline: YouTube TV subscribers offered 50 percent discount on Google streaming device
cards.teaser: Google is providing a promotion to YouTube TV customers for its Google TV Streamer hardware.
cards.body:
Google is offering YouTube TV subscribers a 50 percent discount on the Google TV Streamer, the company's streaming media device. The promotion provides the hardware at half price to customers who subscribe to YouTube TV, Google's live television streaming service.

The Google TV Streamer connects to televisions and allows users to access streaming applications and services. The discount appears designed to encourage YouTube TV subscribers to use Google's hardware rather than competing streaming devices from companies like Roku or Amazon.

hero.headline: Liverpool reaches agreement with Andoni Iraola to replace Arne Slot as head coach
hero.body:
Liverpool have agreed a deal in principle with Andoni Iraola to become their next head coach following the sacking of Arne Slot. The Spaniard has progressed quickly through negotiations with the club's sporting director Richard Hughes and is set to sign a two-year contract at Anfield.

Slot was dismissed with immediate effect after a troubled title defence that saw Liverpool suffer 19 defeats across all competitions. The season was overshadowed by the death of Diogo Jota. Although the club secured Champions League qualification on the final day, Liverpool's hierarchy decided a change in direction was necessary. In a statement, the owners acknowledged the difficulty of the decision but explained that "the team's trajectory is best addressed through a change of direction."

The club invested almost 450 million pounds in new signings last summer but saw significant regression this season. High-profile recruits, including Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak, failed to deliver the expected impact, while established players including Mohamed Salah and Ibrahima Konaté suffered severe drops in form. Problems at set pieces and in open play affected the team throughout the campaign.

Liverpool believe the team's playing style needs to evolve toward a more aggressive, front-foot approach to respond to changes within the Premier League. This tactical vision makes Iraola the clear frontrunner for the position. The Basque coach has built a reputation at Bournemouth for developing attractive, possession-based football since his appointment by Hughes, who now holds the role of sporting director at Liverpool.

Iraola is expected to bring his assistants Tommy Elphick and Shaun Cooper with him from Bournemouth. Both men are under contract at the south coast club, where they valued their experience of playing and coaching in England. However, Bournemouth want them to form part of incoming head coach Marco Rose's staff. The fitness coach Pablo de la Torre, the only staff member Iraola brought from Rayo Vallecano, is out of contract and could make the move.

Iraola faces competition for his signature from other clubs. Milan, Bayer Leverkusen and Crystal Palace have shown interest, but he has not committed to his next role so far.

Liverpool acknowledged that Slot's dismissal appears unfair considering his achievement in winning a record-equalling 20th league title in his first season. The club paid tribute to his handling of the difficult period following Jota's death, describing the compassion and humanity he showed. Slot responded to his departure by saying it had been "an amazing ride" and expressed his gratitude for winning the league.

The club aims to install a replacement quickly as they prepare for the new campaign.

cards.headline: Stephen Curry signs $400 million shoe deal with Li-Ning after leaving Under Armour
cards.teaser: The Golden State Warriors star has agreed to a reported $400 million contract with Chinese footwear company Li-Ning.
cards.body:
Stephen Curry has signed a shoe contract with Chinese company Li-Ning reportedly worth $400 million, marking a major shift after his long partnership with Under Armour ended in 2025. The deal represents one of the largest endorsement agreements in basketball history and a significant win for the Chinese athletic brand.

Curry's move to Li-Ning comes after years as the face of Under Armour's basketball division. According to reports, Curry turned down a larger offer from another company to sign with Li-Ning. The partnership gives the Chinese brand a high-profile ambassador in one of basketball's most popular players.

cards.headline: Manchester United agrees $35 million deal for Atalanta midfielder Ederson
cards.teaser: The Brazilian midfielder is set to become Michael Carrick's first signing as Manchester United manager.
cards.body:
Manchester United has agreed a £35 million deal with Atalanta to sign Brazilian midfielder Ederson, making him Michael Carrick's first signing as permanent manager. The 26-year-old has penned a contract with the club until 2030.

Ederson was identified by Carrick and director of football Jason Wilcox as a replacement for Casemiro, who departed after his contract expired. The signing strengthens United's midfield options as the club continues its transfer activity under Carrick's leadership.

cards.headline: A.J. Brown discusses Eagles tenure and relationship with Jalen Hurts after trade to Patriots
cards.teaser: The wide receiver spoke publicly for the first time since his trade from Philadelphia to New England.
cards.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles traded wide receiver A.J. Brown to the New England Patriots, ending months of speculation about his future. The Eagles received a first-round pick in 2028 and a fifth-round pick in 2027 in the deal for the three-time Pro Bowl selection.

Brown had grown frustrated during his time in Philadelphia. The trade reunites the wideout with Patriots coach Mike Vrabel. Since joining New England, Brown selected the number 1 jersey, declining the opportunity to wear number 11 despite receiving permission from former Patriots receiver Julian Edelman.

cards.headline: Alexander Zverev advances to French Open semifinals with win over Rafael Jodar
cards.teaser: The German player defeated teenager Jodar in straight sets to keep his Grand Slam title hopes alive.
cards.body:
Alexander Zverev reached the French Open semifinals after a comprehensive quarter-final victory over teenage Spanish player Rafael Jodar. The win marks another step in Zverev's ongoing pursuit of his first Grand Slam title.

Zverev will face Jakub Mensik in the semifinals as the tournament progresses toward its conclusion.

cards.headline: Jordan Henderson says England players must acclimatize to Florida heat before World Cup
cards.teaser: The midfielder urged teammates to prepare for sweltering conditions expected at the tournament.
cards.body:
Jordan Henderson has urged England's players to expose themselves to Florida's intense heat in order to acclimatize ahead of the World Cup. The midfielder believes this preparation is essential for the team to be ready for the sweltering conditions expected during the tournament.

Henderson's call emphasizes the importance of heat adaptation in the team's World Cup preparations. By acclimating to Florida's conditions beforehand, England's squad can better prepare themselves for the physical demands they will face competing in the tournament's hot climate.

cards.headline: Charlotte Edwards praises Heather Knight's return to form before T20 World Cup
cards.teaser: The England head coach expressed confidence in the former captain's selection for the tournament.
cards.body:
England head coach Charlotte Edwards has praised Heather Knight's resilience as the former captain returns to form ahead of the T20 World Cup. Edwards expressed confidence in Knight's place within the squad for the tournament.

Knight demonstrated her value to the team in England's recent T20 series victory over India at Taunton. She played a crucial role in a 137-run partnership with Alice Capsey that guided England to a six-wicket win, chasing down India's total of 180 with nine balls remaining. The victory came perfectly timed just 10 days before England's World Cup opener against Sri Lanka on 12 June.

hero.headline: NBC Cancels The Hunting Party After Two Seasons
hero.teaser: The crime drama starring Melissa Roxburgh aired its final episode in May.
hero.body:
NBC has canceled The Hunting Party after two seasons. The series aired its final episode on May 7, ending its run on the network.

The show starred Melissa Roxburgh as Rebecca Bex Henderson, a former FBI profiler who led a team of investigators tracking dangerous criminals. The cancellation follows a pattern of network decisions as the broadcast season concludes.

cards.headline: Singer Peabo Bryson Dies at 75 Following Stroke
cards.teaser: Peabo Bryson, the R&B singer known for performing the title songs for Disney films Beauty and the Beast and Aladdin, has died at 75.
cards.body:
Peabo Bryson, the Grammy-winning R&B singer best known for performing Disney's "Beauty and the Beast" and "A Whole New World," has died at 75. His family announced his passing following a stroke.

Bryson's most recognized work came from his Disney collaborations in the early 1990s. He won two Grammy Awards for "Beauty and the Beast," performed with Celine Dion, and "A Whole New World," performed with Regina Belle. Both songs became signature ballads of the decade. Beyond his Disney success, Bryson built a lengthy R&B career spanning multiple decades with songs including "I'm So Into You" and "Let the Feeling Flow."

cards.headline: Ernest Chambers, Smothers Brothers Comedy Hour Showrunner, Dies at 97
cards.teaser: The television producer and writer died at his Los Angeles home on May 28.
cards.body:
Ernest Chambers, a prolific writer and producer who shaped variety television, died on May 28 at his home in Los Angeles following a brief illness. He was 97.

Over a 50-year career, Chambers produced and wrote more than 1,000 hours of television and earned 11 Emmy nominations. He was best known for his work on "The Smothers Brothers Comedy Hour" and the variety show "Click."

cards.headline: Cassie Ventura Moved Out of United States Following Diddy Settlement
cards.teaser: The singer received a $30 million settlement after her lawsuit against Sean Combs.
cards.body:
Cassie Ventura has revealed she moved out of the United States following her legal settlement with Sean Diddy Combs. The singer received a $30 million settlement after filing a lawsuit against Combs.

The departure came after the conclusion of her legal case, which also involved a trial. Ventura disclosed the move publicly, though she did not specify her current location or indicate whether she plans to return to the country.

cards.headline: Tom Holland and Zendaya Requested Scene Rewrite on Spider-Man Set
cards.teaser: The actors spoke up when a scene in Brand New Day was not working, leading the director to send the crew home.
cards.body:
Tom Holland revealed that he and Zendaya requested a scene rewrite during production of Spider-Man: Brand New Day. The actors told the director a particular scene was not working, prompting the decision to send the crew home so the script could be revised.

Holland discussed working with Zendaya on the latest episode of Amy Poehler's Good Hang podcast, calling it a lifeline and saying he could not imagine doing what he does without her. The two have worked together on four Spider-Man movies, including this summer's Brand New Day, and will both appear in an upcoming project together.

cards.headline: Insomniac Games Details Wolverine Video Game Combat and Mature Content
cards.teaser: Developers discussed new gameplay footage showing the game's blood and gore elements.
cards.body:
Insomniac Games showcased new gameplay footage for its upcoming Marvel's Wolverine, highlighting the game's mature and bloody combat. Creative director Marcus Smith emphasized to Variety that the studio is making a clear statement about the game's mature rating.

The developers revealed several gameplay elements including X-Men cameos, a low-gore option for players who prefer less graphic content, and claw-based combat mechanics. The game will also feature sequences where Logan can die, bringing his violent nature to life in interactive form. The PlayStation exclusive demonstrates Insomniac's commitment to capturing Wolverine's brutal character through gameplay.

cards.headline: Mindy Kaling Discusses Gen-Z Workplace Comedy Not Suitable For Work
cards.teaser: The producer and star spoke about depicting younger workers and setting up multiple love triangles in the Hulu series.
cards.body:
Mindy Kaling's new Hulu series Not Suitable For Work follows five twentysomethings living across two Manhattan apartments as they navigate work, relationships, and life in the city. The show features characters more diverse than classic sitcoms that preceded it, with two main characters of color.

Kaling and the show's creative team deliberately crafted multiple romantic entanglements throughout the series to keep audiences uncertain about relationship outcomes. The deliberate approach to depicting the Gen-Z workforce reflects Kaling's recent success with university-focused comedy The Sex Lives of College Girls and high school sitcom Never Have I Ever.

hero.headline: Illinois senators call for Chicago US attorney to resign
hero.teaser: Sens. Dick Durbin and Tammy Duckworth demanded interim U.S. Attorney Andrew Boutros step down after a failed prosecution.
hero.body:
Illinois Sens. Dick Durbin and Tammy Duckworth called for interim U.S. Attorney Andrew Boutros to resign on Tuesday. The two Democratic senators accused Boutros of presiding over a federal office marked by dysfunction and alleged misconduct.

The call for resignation followed the collapse of the Broadview Six case. Boutros serves as interim U.S. Attorney for the Northern District of Illinois, which includes Chicago and surrounding areas.

cards.headline: Jeffries declines to endorse Wasserman Schultz in rare break from tradition
cards.teaser: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries said he has not decided whether to support Rep. Debbie Wasserman Schultz's reelection bid.
cards.body:
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries said Tuesday he has not yet decided whether to back Rep. Debbie Wasserman Schultz for reelection. The Florida Democrat faces anger over her decision to run in a majority-minority district.

The move stunned House Democrats, who noted Jeffries typically supports all incumbents regardless of controversy. One senior House Democrat told Axios that Jeffries has never withheld an endorsement before. Jeffries himself said Tuesday in response to another question that he stands behind every member.

cards.headline: California holds primary for governor as Newsom term ends
cards.teaser: Democrats Katie Porter, Tom Steyer and Xavier Becerra face Republicans Chad Bianco and Steve Hilton in the race to replace Gov. Gavin Newsom.
cards.body:
California voters are casting ballots Tuesday in a competitive gubernatorial primary featuring Democrats Katie Porter, Tom Steyer and Xavier Becerra, and Republicans Chad Bianco and Steve Hilton. The race will determine who replaces outgoing Gov. Gavin Newsom.

The state's top-two primary system places all candidates on a single ballot, with the top two vote-getters advancing to the general election regardless of party. Election experts warn that California's vote-counting process could delay final results for days or weeks, as county elections offices process a deluge of last-minute absentee ballots through a detailed verification procedure.

cards.headline: New Mexico holds governor primary with Biden Cabinet member Haaland on ballot
cards.teaser: Interior Secretary Deb Haaland is among five candidates seeking their party's nomination to replace Gov. Michelle Lujan Grisham.
cards.body:
New Mexico voters are choosing Democratic and Republican nominees for governor on Tuesday. The Democratic primary features Interior Secretary Deb Haaland alongside challengers Sam Bregman, Gregg Hull, Duke Rodriguez and Doug Turner. The winner will face off to replace term-limited Governor Michelle Lujan Grisham.

Haaland, who previously represented New Mexico's 1st congressional district in the House, joined President Biden's Cabinet as head of the Interior Department before entering the gubernatorial race.

cards.headline: Maine Senate candidate Platner meets with Democrats amid scandals
cards.teaser: Democratic Senate candidate Graham Platner sought support from Senate Democrats as he faces fresh scrutiny over sexually explicit messages.
cards.body:
Maine Democratic Senate candidate Graham Platner met with Senate Democrats at Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee headquarters in Washington on Tuesday. The meeting lasted more than an hour and a half as Platner sought to maintain support for his campaign to flip the seat.

Platner is facing mounting controversies. Recent reports revealed he sent sexually explicit messages. Previously, he cited PTSD in relation to racist, sexist and homophobic online posts, and covered up a Nazi tattoo. Platner declined to answer reporters' questions as he left the meeting.

cards.headline: Ex-Obama aide warns Los Angeles Mayor Bass faces tough reelection
cards.teaser: Democratic strategist Jim Messina said Mayor Karen Bass should be concerned about her chances regardless of who advances to the runoff.
cards.body:
Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass should be worried about her reelection prospects no matter which opponent she faces in a runoff, according to Democratic strategist Jim Messina. The former White House deputy chief of staff under President Obama made the assessment ahead of the California primary on Tuesday.

Bass, a Democrat, is seeking a second term as mayor of the nation's second-largest city. California's nonpartisan primary system allows the top two vote-getters to advance to a runoff election.

cards.headline: Judge blocks NOTUS news outlet from rebranding as The Star
cards.teaser: A federal judge issued a temporary restraining order blocking the news outlet's rebrand after a lawsuit from The Washington Star.
cards.body:
District Judge Rossie D. Alston Jr. issued a temporary restraining order on Tuesday preventing NOTUS news outlet from rebranding as The Star. The decision came after The Washington Star filed a lawsuit challenging the name change.

The judge ordered both news outlets to schedule a settlement conference within seven days, with another hearing to follow on the matter.
